# RR133: proper-support selection with its exact joint law and zero-mass boundary

2026-10-15 UTC. Fixed author-side local paper support, not a new Native
execution or terminal Task result. Original RR133 owner/author attribution
and current researcher EM-N-DEA587 (prior contribution EM-DVR-F27A61) are
preserved. Root EM-DVR-FBF223 directed a concrete continuation beyond the
completed existential observer; this note's particular rejection-law and
zero-mass construction were developed by the current researcher. Exposure
is DIRECTED_SHARED_CONTEXT_NONBLIND. No old run or lease is used as current
authority, and no new owner, claim or run is created.

**New bounded result.** On the already bound explicit-terminal probabilistic
slice, proper-support selection has a public implementation that preserves
the ENTIRE original terminal law conditional on proper support. It needs
positive success probability but no supplied positive lower bound. In the
same effective finite-output envelope, deciding that this probability is
zero is uniformly impossible, even when every supplied program halts almost
surely and every terminal support test is total. This second statement is
a precise decision boundary, not an admitted escape, a specification gap,
a failure of simulation, or a factoring impossibility theorem.

## 1. Actual Source binding and the open slot completed here

The saved current Task at Source a2b4f908009eda28ccfef8638dda7ab28f856ecd,
research_tasks/RR133_COVERAGE_PROSPECTIVE_GEN2.md, retains explicit finite
presentations (line 80), exact public seed-law externalization (83), and
public effective almost-sure computation (84). Lines 87-89 allow correctly
typed derived operational descriptions and require symmetric public
availability. Lines 99-103 require preservation of the relevant terminal
presentation/readout. These do not grant arbitrary postselection as an
oracle. We provide an implementation of one specified selection operator.

The historical, still-preserved G_effect-dist^eff contract supplies a
public computable interpreter, public effective random tape, almost-sure
termination and finite explicit presentation output. The current RRBF7
return sections 4-6 establishes the exact joint-readout and support scope;
it is an input, not a theorem rerun here.

The reviewed 056 proper-support unit defines the total public readout

    Q_N(C,a)=(C,a,delta,u,tau,Proper_N(C)),             (1)

where C=(r,e,A) presents coker(A:(Z/NZ)^e -> (Z/NZ)^r), delta is the
inherited determinantal gcd, u is its computed complementary saturation,
tau=N/u, and

    Proper_N(C) iff Supp_N(C) is nonempty and
                       strictly contained in Pr(N). (2)

All degenerate and nonsquarefree cases are handled by the inherited total
test. We do not
rerun or reprove its gcd loop, CRT valuation argument or determinant test.

That same 056 unit, section 5 lines 220-227, explicitly says its c.e.
witness finder does NOT preserve an original distribution and is not a
conditional/postselected sampler. That is the precise existing unfilled
slot addressed here. A new candidate Phi with an unlocated interface is
not needed for this bounded slice, and no R059D search is performed.

## 2. Complete operator interface, including the reset condition

Input is public (N,P), N>=2. All additional finite public initial-state
data are part of P's specification (or effectively obtained from N), not
hidden factor-correlated advice. P is in the stated effective probabilistic
class and returns a finite joint terminal code

    Z=(C,a)

almost surely. C has the explicit type above. The retained a contains
the DECLARED joint annotations/observations and any terminal state required
by the scoped future operations. Neither a support mask nor C's marginal
distribution is substituted for this joint code. A program that returns
only an opaque handle without this terminal interface is outside this
unit's hypothesis.

Specify the derived operation SelectProper(N,P) as follows:

1. Execute P from its specified complete initial state using a fresh
   independent fair-bit tape (or its already licensed inlined sampler).
2. On its finite output Z=(C,a), compute the total test Proper_N(C).
3. If true, return Q_N(C,a); otherwise start a fresh trial from that SAME
   specified initial state with independent random resources.

This is a public algorithm on the public program specification. Reset
means creating another interpreter execution, with all mutable state
owned by that trial initialized as specified. It is not a physical reset
or cloning axiom for an arbitrary resource. Persistent shared environment
state, cached randomness intended to persist BETWEEN trials, or hidden
latent conditioning data must not be erased by fiat. If such state is
part of the actual requested operation, it must be represented in its
contract; the independent-trial operator above is a different operation
unless its reset is justified. Within each trial all dependencies and
random-address caches of P remain intact.

The output is a fresh accepted terminal, not the realized private branch
of some earlier execution. The algorithm tests support only AFTER that
terminal has been produced; it supplies no hidden CRT selector to P.

## 3. Exact conditional-joint-law theorem

Let mu be the probability law of Z from one trial. Let

    E={z=(C,a): Proper_N(C)}, q=mu(E).                (3)

**Theorem 1.** For every promised input above with q>0, SelectProper is a
public almost-surely terminating program. For every set B of finite joint
terminal codes, its accepted terminal Z_* satisfies

    Pr[Z_* in B] = mu(B intersect E)/q.              (4)

Its complete output has law Q_N applied to this conditional JOINT law.
No known lower bound on q, probability table, expected-time bound, factor
oracle or call to a zero-probability decision procedure is required.

*Proof.* Couple the trials to a sequence of independent random tapes,
thus to i.i.d. outputs Z_1,Z_2,... with law mu. Each trial is finite with
probability one. The countable union of their nontermination null events
has probability zero. For K, the first index with Z_K in E,

    Pr[K>j]=(1-q)^j -> 0.

Thus K is finite almost surely. On the event that K is finite and its
finitely many preceding trials terminate, the serial program also finishes:
a finite sum of finite runtimes and total readout computations is finite.
No expectation interchange or tail-rate hypothesis is used.

By independence, for every integer j>=1,

    Pr[K=j and Z_j in B]=(1-q)^(j-1) mu(B intersect E).

These disjoint events sum to mu(B intersect E)/q, proving (4). Applying
the deterministic total joint map Q_N proves the full output assertion.
This is a proof about a program defined without q; the geometric sum in
the proof is not an implementation instruction. QED.

For q=1 it simply returns the first trial. For q=0 a conditional law on E
is not specified by (4), and the program is not promised to terminate.
In the finite-bit model any actual finite halting trace has a positive
cylinder measure, so q=0 also precludes a legal finite successful trace;
the inherited support theorem already establishes this fact. No negative
answer is inferred from a long unsuccessful search.

This preserves the accepted terminal's original conditional distribution,
not the original unconditional distribution. If one additionally returns
K or the rejected-trial log, those are new coordinates with the law of the
wrapper experiment; they are not a claimed reconstruction of an original
single-run history. In particular (4) applies to the retained (C,a) jointly,
not to separately resampled annotations or marginal support values.

The old generic emulator now applies to this actual algorithm on q>0:
external and runtime executions have the same conditional joint law.
There is no unexplained conditioning oracle left in this operator. This
does not identify its computation time with that of the original P or of
any other mechanism. A trial can have infinite expected runtime despite
almost-sure termination, and q can be arbitrarily small.

## 4. What the earlier probability certificate adds, without rerunning it

Compose one trial of P with its total Boolean Proper readout, returning
0 or 1. This remains an almost-surely terminating fair-bit program. The
already completed 048 converse theorem therefore gives uniform rational
approximations to q from (N,P) on the stated promise domain. Its existing
finite-tree proof is not repeated or executed here.

Strict positivity can be semidecided by searching those sound intervals
for a positive lower bound. That optional proof certificate is not needed
by SelectProper. Computability of the real q does not make its equality
to zero decidable. The following explicit family fixes that distinction
inside the actual finite-presentation terminal type.

There is also a finite operational certificate for q>0: an actual legal
terminating trace from the specified initial state, with k consumed fresh
bits, explicit terminal (C,a), and Proper_N(C)=true. All tapes extending
that consumed prefix have the same successful finite computation, so
q>=2^(-k). Thus a single such trace discharges the positive-mass promise
without finding q or deciding all possible branches. This is an application
of the already proved finite-cylinder support argument, not a new trace
execution. It cannot be replaced by an arbitrary semantic witness or by
a presentation not produced by that actual P. No runtime bound is added
to the Task.

## 5. A new exact zero-mass boundary with entirely effective terminals

**Theorem 2.** There is no total computable procedure that, given every
program in this public almost-surely terminating finite-presentation
envelope, decides whether its proper-support probability q is zero.
This assertion is about that general EFFECTIVE PROGRAM ENVELOPE, not the
still-unclassified subclass of admissible new nonclassical mechanisms.

*Proof.* Fix the public composite N=6 once and for all. Two fixed terminal
presentations are

    C_0=(1,1,[1]), C_1=(1,1,[2]).                    (5)

C_0 presents the zero module and has empty residue support. C_1 presents
(Z/6Z)/2(Z/6Z); its residue support is {2}, strictly contained in {2,3}.
Thus Proper_6(C_0)=false and Proper_6(C_1)=true. The label can be one
fixed finite symbol a_0 in both cases. These are exact algebraic facts,
not executed matrix samples or a proposed factoring mechanism.

Given a deterministic machine index k, effectively construct P_k:

* Read fair bits until the first 1, and let T be the number of preceding
  zeros. Thus T ranges over nonnegative integers with
  Pr[T=t]=2^(-(t+1)).
* Simulate machine k on its fixed empty input for at most T elementary
  transitions, including a check of whether the initial state is halted.
* Return (C_1,a_0) if halting has occurred within that budget; otherwise
  return (C_0,a_0).

Each P_k is uniformly public and has no unbounded machine-halting test:
the simulation after drawing T is explicitly bounded. The all-zero tape
has probability zero. For every other tape T is finite, so the bounded
simulation and explicit terminal output finish. Therefore EVERY P_k
halts almost surely, whether or not machine k ever halts.

If k has first halting time h>=0, then it returns C_1 exactly when T>=h;
if k never halts it never returns C_1. Hence

    q_k=2^(-h) if k halts first at h,
    q_k=0      if k never halts.                    (6)

A purported total zero-mass decider on this promised class would decide
nonhalting, and its complement would decide halting, a contradiction.
It suffices that the decider terminate on all promised codes: every P_k
constructed above belongs to the promise class, independently of k.
No undecidable semantic equality of a terminal object was used. QED.

For completeness, q_k is UNIFORMLY COMPUTABLE despite this obstruction.
To approximate it within 2^(-n), simulate k for n transitions (checking
time zero). If it halts at h<=n, output 2^(-h); otherwise output 0. Any
later first halt has h>=n+1 and contributes at most 2^(-(n+1)); a machine
that never halts contributes zero. This is a paper specification and
proof of an approximation algorithm, not an executed simulation.

The fixed N=6 and coefficient 2 are openly supplied constants, not hidden
factor-correlated input. But the example is explicitly direct-nonunit
terminal selection and is NOT offered as a surviving mechanism under the
Objective's novelty/firewall requirements. It shows why a generic coverage
translation need not decide success or nonexistence in its source program
class. It does not prove such undecidability for every narrower admissible
candidate grammar, and is not a reduction of the factoring problem.

This is different from the completed c.e.-quotient pressure test: there,
a finite index named a completed semantic quotient whose support lacked
a uniform effective finite-presentation compiler. Here every individual
execution finishes with one of TWO explicit matrices and the properness
observer is total. The undecidable statement quantifies over the whole
program's possible executions, not over an opaque terminal interpretation.

## 6. Classification, exact increment and next input/output boundary

The concrete derived operation classified is positive-mass proper-support
conditioning of an already licensed, resettable public effective generator
with explicit joint terminals. Its input and executable implementation
are (N,P) and Section 2; its output guarantee is the exact law (4) followed
by (1). It is covered on q>0. A separately declared operation that returns
the same law instantly or answers a zero-mass case is NOT licensed merely
by this theorem; any claimed stronger semantics needs its own actual
contract and escape classification.

Under the inherited prior-art review this wrapper is ordinary repeated
presentation/nonunit search at an effective endpoint, not a new source of
asymmetric singularity. It does not turn a prior-art-equivalent P into a
novel mechanism, nor does a final gcd by itself invalidate some distinct
generation mechanism inside P. Generation, observation and extraction
remain separately typed as the Objective requires.

Bounded dedup used the current RRBF7 return, finite-presentation application,
056 proper observer, 048 kernel/converse, c.e.-quotient note and the saved
Phi quotation map. The exact missing conditional-law sentence of 056 is
now discharged on the stated probabilistic slice. Rejection sampling and
the computability reduction are standard mathematical methods; there is
no global novelty claim or new general-purpose checker/tool family.

For a subsequent specific binding, the required input is one actual
generator P with its complete initial-state/reset contract and explicit
terminal (C,a), plus a source-derived q>0 witness or promise if conditional
termination is claimed. The output is a certified conditional joint-law
implementation, not just a reachable witness. If the input supplies only
nondeterministic c.e. branches, no probability law is invented; the old
existential result remains the appropriate conclusion. If the input is
only a semantic handle or lacks reset, this note makes no unsupported
translation for it.

All-source resource coverage, a genuine escape, a specification-gap result
and parent closure remain OPEN. Theorem 2 is not a reason to demand a
zero-mass oracle before proving a coverage translation. No optional cost
bound is made a new hard target, and no absent locator is treated as proof
that a permitted primitive cannot exist.

The existing temporary collaborator crt_bound_adversarial_read checked

count and total runtime. That is disclosed author-side assistance, not

Only saved-source reads, paper proofs, local text persistence and hashing
